sections.heading: The Citronelle field's long shadow
paragraphs: Discovered in 1955 and developed heavily through the following decades, the Citronelle oil field became one of the largest onshore oil discoveries in Alabama history, producing from sands associated with the Citronelle salt dome at relatively shallow depth. Many mineral interests across this part of Mobile County trace their leasing history back to that development boom, even on tracts that were never directly drilled.

Production from the core of the field has declined significantly from its peak decades ago, but some wells continue producing at low, stripper-well volumes today, which still generates real, if modest, royalty income for the mineral owners tied to them.

sections.heading: Checking your Grand Bay tract against the field

That comparison tells us whether your interest has an actual production history to value or falls into the more speculative, undeveloped category.
Either way, we will explain clearly which situation applies to you before discussing a number.

faqs.question: Is Grand Bay actually part of the Citronelle oil field?
faqs.answer: Parts of southwest Mobile County near Grand Bay sit within or close to the historic field boundaries; we check your specific legal description to confirm.

faqs.question: Is the Citronelle field still producing today?
faqs.answer: Yes, though at much lower, stripper-well volumes than during its peak decades ago, which still generates modest royalty income for some owners.

faqs.question: What if my family's tract was leased but never actually drilled?
faqs.answer: That is common on the edges of a large field like Citronelle; we evaluate these interests conservatively based on proximity to actual production.

faqs.question: How do I find my family's original Citronelle-era lease?
faqs.answer: It would typically be recorded with the Mobile County Probate Office, and we can help locate it if you do not have your own copy.
